To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adsorption of pharmaceuticals can be greatly enhanced by activating AC with potassium hydroxides, carbon dioxide, or steam.
the adsorption of pharmaceuticals on microporous activated carbons can be greatly enhanced by activating treatments that enlarge pore size, especially when the adsorbates are large in size.

activation treatments of AC can significantly improve adsorption of bulky antibiotics to AC by enlarging the pore size, but not for low-size adsorbates due to the dominance of micropore filling effect.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
activation treatments can greatly enhance the adsorption of pharmaceuticals with a molecular diameter of > 1 nm to AC, but not for pharmaceuticals with molecular diameters < 1 nm.
the adsorbent surface area and the pore size distribution are the two key factors in adsorption of pharmaceuticals onto microporous AC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adsorption of pharmaceuticals is mainly controlled by their size, with the adsorption of low-sized compounds dominated by micropore-fills effect and the adsorption of high-sized compounds by the combination of micropore-fill and mesopore-fill effects.
the activation of microporous adsorbents for efficient adsorption of pharmaceuticals can be achieved by balancing the micropore-filing effect with the size-exclusion effect.

microporous activated carbons are not suitable for the removal of large-size pharmaceuticals from aqueous solutions due to their size-exclusion effect, and the removal efficiency of these pharmaceuticals could be greatly improved by enlarging the pore size of the adsorbents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microporous activated carbons can be tailored for the removal of pharmaceuticals from water by optimizing their porosity through activation treatments.
the pore-size dependent adsorptive behaviors of pharmaceuticals should be considered in the design of efficient adsorbents.
the adsorbent selection for pharmaceuticals in aqueous media should take into consideration their molecular sizes.
